summary: The appellant was convicted for murder under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and destruction of evidence under Section 201 IPC based solely on extra-judicial confession. The prosecution relied on three witnesses (PW-7, PW-8, PW-9) who claimed the appellant confessed, but their testimonies were inconsistent, uncorroborated, and lacked naturalness. The Court held that extra-judicial confession must be voluntary, reliable, and made to persons with whom the accused has trust; mere recovery of bodies without confirmation by investigation or corroboration was insufficient. The Court found no reliable evidence supporting the confession and no other incriminating circumstances.
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; conviction set aside; appellant acquitted; bail bonds cancelled.
